metadata.case_name: RUKHSAR BEGUM v. NATIVE ENGLISH CENTER LTD T/A THE GREEN LOUNGE

injuries.description: Fracture of the base of the distal phalanx of the right ring finger (healed with mild mal-union).
source: Dr Li found, after reviewing the X–ray films of the right ring finger, that there was in fact a fracture of the base of the distal phalanx of the finger even though the fracture had already healed quite well with mild mal-union at the time of his review of the films.
TB p.86: "right ring finger ... mild stiffness"

injuries.description: Meniscal tear of the right knee (classified as "grade 2"); right traumatic patellar tendinitis; right knee pain with decreased range of motion.
source: It was stated in the MRI report that the knee had a "possible tear of posterior horn of medical meniscus".
Dr Li classified the meniscal tear of the right knee as "grade 2".
TB p.85: complaints of pain in the right knee with a decreased range of motion.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of other specified muscle, fascia, tendon or bursa at lower leg level

manifestations.description: Tender and swollen right ring finger and right knee
Mild stiffness of right ring finger
Discomfort from continuous bending or standing for 4 hours or more; unable to stand for more than 4 hours

treatments_received: Treated and discharged from A&E with a knee brace and walking stick
Four follow-up sessions with the Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department of Queen Mary Hospital on 2 December 2013, 24 February 2014, 3 March 2014 and 23 June 2014
Two physiotherapy treatments for knee injury on 16 and 23 December 2013
MRI scan of the right knee (15 January 2014) done privately
treatments_future: Home exercises using "Power Putty" (recommended by Dr Li)

losses.description: Unable to resume her pre-accident waitressing job due to residual pain from the knee.
Mild mal-union of the base of the distal phalanx of the right ring finger which may potentially cause residual symptoms.
